text:
amelia: Thanks everyone — following up from the pricing segment in today's All Hands. Using this thread to capture Qs about rate limits, quotas, and credits. I (and raj/leo) will answer live and follow up after.

natalie: quick one — do free trial credits expire? and will the console warn users before they vanish?

leo: short answer: yes, trial credits expire. Current policy = 90 days from issue. Console shows a banner and an expiry date on the Billing page. For enterprise customers we can discuss extensions case-by-case.

natalie: ok thanks — can we get an explicit expiry column in the CSV export? that's what partners asked for.

leo: noted, adding to backlog. Will try to include in the May billing export.

jin: rate limits question from infra folks — what's the per-key concurrency & burst behavior for hosted API? any graceful degradation rules?

raj: default hosted policy: conservative defaults to protect multi-tenant clusters. Current defaults: 60 rps and 16 concurrent requests per API key for text generation. We allow short bursts (up to ~120 rps) via a soft-burst window if cluster has spare capacity — but bursts are not guaranteed. When limits hit, clients receive 429 with Retry-After.

jin: is there a way to request higher limits for specific keys?

olivia: yes — growth/enterprise customers can request quota increases via the billing form. For Dedicated customers, we expose reserved throughput in the Console and those requests are part of the Dedicated sizing/contract.

natalie: related — how do credits interact with bursts? example: if I'm at rate limit but I have credits, do they let me exceed limits?

raj: important distinction: credits are currency (payee) not a control plane knob. Credits pay for overage (or usage) but they do not bypass rate/concurrency limits. We do use credits for billing (e.g., charging for overages), but rate limits are enforced to protect service stability. The exception is some enterprise-level negotiated burst allowances configured in contract and implemented on the routing policy.

amelia: TL;DR: credits = money, quotas/rate limits = safety. We'll avoid mixing the two unless explicitly contracted.

olivia: also a common ask — can unused committed credits from Dedicated roll over month-to-month?

leo: committed capacity billing and crediting has two flavors: reserved capacity (Dedicated) is contracted; unused reserved hours cannot be converted to hosted credits by default. For customers on annual contracts we offer rollover in special cases; it's negotiated in the contract appendix. We'll add clearer language to the pricing docs.

natalie: can you paste where console shows credits? people keep asking.

raj: Console path: "Billing → Credits & Usage". The page shows current balance, pending promotions, and expiry dates. CLI check: ```redwood billing credits --org my-org``` (prototype CLI). Docs: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/billing/credits (internal-preview).

jin: follow-up about programmatic quotas — is there an API to read per-key quota and usage in realtime?

raj: we have a usage API returning hourly token counts and active connections. It's rate-limited itself. We're migrating to expose a "quota" endpoint that returns the effective limits for a key (post-policy evaluation) — ETA: end of Q2.

natalie: customers also asked for alerting when usage is near quota (like 80%). Is that on roadmap?

leo: yes, email/webhook alerts at 50/80/95% are planned. We'll ship basic thresholds in the May release and add custom thresholds later.

olivia: question from sales — for pilot customers, can we offer temporary elevated burst for demos? what's the process?

raj: Ops can toggle a demo policy for a short window. Please file a support ticket referencing the demo key and desired window. We'll need business justification for bursts > default.

amelia: action items: (1) leo to draft clear public billing FAQ about expiry/rollover by next week, (2) raj to publish quota endpoint ETA and sample responses, (3) natalie to collect top 5 billing UI asks from sales/SEs and prioritize.

deploy-bot: New billing UI feature flag will roll out to 25% of accounts on 2026-05-12.

natalie: thanks — can you @me when the feature flag is live? I'll coordinate comms. :thumbsup:

leo: will do.

amelia: great thread — keep questions coming and we'll update the internal KB after the follow-ups.
